overview: Seven & i Holdings is a Tokyo-listed pure holding company centered on convenience-store retailing, operating 7-Eleven Japan (SEJ) domestically and 7-Eleven, Inc. (including Speedway, acquired 2021) across North America, Australia and China. Following the September 2025 divestiture of its superstore/specialty businesses (Ito-Yokado, York-Benimaru, LOFT, Akachan Honpo, Denny's Japan) to a Bain Capital-led vehicle and the deconsolidation of Seven Bank in June 2025, the company has become a far more focused, pure-play global convenience-store operator than at any point in the last two decades. It generates revenue predominantly through franchised and company-operated convenience stores selling food, beverages, fuel and daily goods, supplemented by royalty income from franchisees.

business_model.summary: Revenue is earned mainly from (1) direct merchandise and fuel sales at company-operated stores and at 7-Eleven, Inc.'s larger owned store base in North America, and (2) royalty/franchise fees from the vast majority of SEJ's Japanese stores, which are franchised to independent operators. Gasoline sales are a meaningful, low-margin, high-revenue contributor in North America. Revenue is largely transactional/retail (daily repeat footfall) rather than subscription-based, but the franchise royalty stream behaves like a recurring, high-margin annuity tied to same-store sales. Post-FY2026 restructuring, the group is reported in two core segments -- domestic convenience store operations and overseas convenience store operations -- after superstore operations shrank from ~13% to residual scale and Seven Bank moved off the balance sheet.

revenue_streams.name: Overseas convenience stores (7-Eleven Inc./Speedway, Australia, China)
Domestic convenience stores (SEJ)
revenue_streams.trend: stable, but domestic CVS operating income has drifted down from JPY250.5bn (FY2024) to JPY222.5bn (FY2026)

revenue_streams.name: Superstore operations (residual, post-YORK deconsolidation)
revenue_streams.trend: sharply declining -- fell from JPY1.43trn to JPY689bn in FY2026 after YORK Holdings sale

revenue_streams.name: Financial services / other (Seven Bank equity income, Seven Card, etc.)
revenue_streams.trend: declining -- Seven Bank deconsolidated June 2025, now equity-method

business_model.customer_type: B2C mass-market convenience retail; B2B relationship with franchisees (SEJ) who operate the majority of Japanese stores under royalty agreements
business_model.geographic_mix: FY2026: Overseas (mainly North America) ~82% of consolidated revenue (JPY8.56trn of JPY10.43trn), Domestic convenience stores ~76% of revenue on a segment basis (note segments overlap/are not mutually exclusive in the filing), superstore (Japan) residual ~7%, other ~2%. North America is the single largest external geography by far given 7-Eleven Inc./Speedway's scale.

competitive_position.market_position: Clear #1 convenience store operator in Japan by sales (historically ~40%+ share) and store count (~21,000+ domestic stores); 7-Eleven, Inc. is the largest convenience store chain in the U.S./Canada by store count, but faces intensifying competition from fuel-focused and larger-format chains (Wawa, Sheetz, Buc-ee's, Casey's) that are taking share in fresh food and fuel margin.

moat_factors.description: The 7-Eleven brand is globally recognized with unmatched store density in Japan and a leading U.S. store count; Japan's top-3 chains (7-Eleven, Lawson, FamilyMart) control ~90% of the convenience store market, giving SEJ purchasing and logistics scale advantages
SEJ's royalty-based franchise model in Japan provides high-margin, capital-light recurring income and strong franchisee density/site selection discipline built over decades

moat_factors.factor: Private-label merchandise (Seven Premium) and fresh-food supply chain
moat_factors.description: Proprietary fresh/prepared food development (onigiri, bento, Seven Café) differentiates from pure fuel-and-snack competitors and drives repeat visits and higher gross margin mix
Decades of site selection in Japan and the acquired Speedway network in the U.S. create switching costs for franchisees and difficult-to-replicate convenience locations

weaknesses: North American business has been losing momentum: FY2026 saw U.S. same-store merchandise sales decline and 7-Eleven Inc. chain sales down 7.3%, with fuel demand also pressured
Overexposure to gasoline/fuel sales in North America, a structurally challenged category amid EV transition and fuel-margin volatility
Historically complex conglomerate structure (now simplified, but execution risk remains in completing the transformation)
Japan's demographic decline (aging/shrinking population) constrains organic same-store growth in the core domestic market
Newer, larger-format U.S. rivals (Wawa, Sheetz, Buc-ee's) are out-executing on fresh food and store experience in some regions

growth_drivers: "Transformation of 7-Eleven" global strategic plan (announced August 2025) -- a unified global brand strategy with reformed management processes, speed and accountability

North Star plan for the North American business: store remodels, expanded franchising, ~645 underperforming store closures vs. ~205 new openings (net reduction ~440) in FY2026, with over 200 larger-format stores planned for the following year to compete with Wawa/Sheetz/Buc-ee's
Approximately JPY300 billion investment in higher-value fresh/prepared food ("Live Meal" line), with SEVEN CAFÉ Bakery targeted at ~18,000 stores and SEVEN CAFÉ Tea at ~10,000 stores
Domestic store network expansion target of approximately 1,000 additional Japanese stores by FY2030, including compact-format stores and expansion into sparsely populated areas
7NOW delivery service expansion (approximately 7,500 U.S. stores) and continued loyalty program (7Rewards) growth
Europe targeted as the group's "fourth major growth pillar" via 7-Eleven International LLC's equity-model market entry and concentrated store openings
Potential future IPO/partial listing of the North American business (pushed back to at least FY2027) to crystallize value and sharpen capital allocation
Large capital return program -- JPY600 billion buyback executed in FY2026, more to follow through the multi-year plan -- supporting EPS growth as share count shrinks

business.description: FY2026 U.S. same-store merchandise sales declined and chain sales fell 7.3%; management cites inflation-squeezed consumers and high gasoline prices reducing driving/visits
Wawa, Sheetz, Buc-ee's and Casey's are winning share in fresh food and larger-format convenience, pressuring 7-Eleven Inc.'s positioning

business.risk: Execution risk of Transformation Plan / North Star plan
business.description: Store closures/remodels, franchising expansion and new management processes must be executed by a largely new leadership team following the 2025 restructuring

business.risk: Domestic market saturation and demographic decline
business.description: Japan's shrinking, aging population structurally limits organic same-store growth; domestic CVS operating income already down from JPY250.5bn (FY2024) to JPY222.5bn (FY2026)

financial.risk: Balance sheet/continuity break from YORK and Seven Bank deconsolidation
financial.description: Cash, debt and equity are not comparable FY2025-to-FY2026: cash fell from JPY1.35trn to JPY426bn, total assets from JPY11.4trn to JPY9.1trn, reflecting the ~JPY813bn of banking deposits/ATM cash removed with Seven Bank's deconsolidation and the YORK Holdings sale -- flagged for anyone modeling trailing growth or liquidity ratios across this boundary
Majority of revenue now overseas (largely USD-denominated North American operations), creating translation and economic exposure to yen/dollar moves

financial.risk: Large buyback funded partly by divestiture proceeds
financial.description: JPY600bn FY2026 buyback and a multi-year ~JPY2 trillion program reduce financial flexibility if North American turnaround underperforms or capex needs rise

regulatory.risk: U.S. antitrust scrutiny of large convenience-store combinations
regulatory.description: Cited by Seven & i itself as a reason the Couche-Tard transaction would have faced extraordinary antitrust hurdles in the U.S.; any future large M&A faces similar scrutiny
Company explicitly flags regional divergence in EV adoption and potential restrictions on gasoline vehicle sales as a medium-term risk to fuel revenue and store traffic

regulatory.risk: Food safety/labeling and data protection regulation across many jurisdictions
regulatory.description: Diversified global footprint (Japan, U.S., Australia, China, aspirational Europe) creates a patchwork of compliance requirements

macro.description: Management cites a 'defensive consumer mindset' in Japan and inflation-squeezed U.S. consumers as headwinds to discretionary and fuel-linked spending
Fuel margins are a swing factor in North American profitability (Q1 FY2027 strength was fuel-margin driven); structurally, gasoline demand risks long-term decline
Company's own risk disclosure highlights political change, protectionism and trade friction affecting its multi-country footprint (Japan, US, Australia, China)

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Japan's convenience store industry is mature and consolidated (top 3 chains ~90% of sales) with limited unit growth but stable royalty economics; the U.S. convenience/fuel retail industry is more fragmented and competitively dynamic, with larger-format, fresh-food-focused chains (Wawa, Sheetz, Buc-ee's) gaining share from traditional players including 7-Eleven.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate -- convenience retail (food, daily goods) is relatively defensive, but fuel volumes/margins and discretionary prepared-food spend have some sensitivity to consumer and gasoline-price cycles
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-to-moderate direct exposure; large capital return program (buybacks) and real estate/store investment could be more costly to finance in a higher-rate environment, and the YORK/Seven Bank deconsolidations have reshaped the balance sheet materially
key_input_costs: Food and agricultural raw materials (fresh/prepared food)
Labor (store staffing amid Japan's manpower shortage)

recent_developments.event: Alimentation Couche-Tard withdrew its roughly USD47 billion ($20.00/share-equivalent, revised from an initial ~$38-58bn range of proposals) unsolicited takeover proposal for Seven & i, citing a lack of constructive engagement from the board; Seven & i disputed Couche-Tard's characterization but did not contest the withdrawal. Couche-Tard reiterated it would not pursue a hostile bid.

Stephen Hayes Dacus, previously board chairman and lead independent outside director, became President, Representative Director and CEO, succeeding Ryuichi Isaka -- the first foreign executive to lead the company; Junro Ito transitioned to Executive Chair.

Seven Bank, Ltd. was deconsolidated (24 June 2025) and became an equity-method affiliate after Seven & i sold down its stake, removing roughly JPY813bn of banking deposits and most ATM cash from the consolidated balance sheet.
Management unveiled the "Transformation of 7-Eleven" global strategic plan -- the company's first truly global strategy -- alongside a shift to a convenience-store-focused organizational structure.

Completed the absorption-type split/sale of YORK Holdings (Ito-Yokado, York-Benimaru, LOFT, Akachan Honpo, Denny's Japan) to a Bain Capital-led vehicle (~JPY814.7bn deal value) with Seven & i and the Ito family retaining a reinvestment stake via equity-method affiliate K.K. BCJ-95; superstore segment revenue fell from JPY1.43trn to JPY689bn for FY2026, with a JPY26.9bn gain recognized on the change in equity interest.

FY2026 (ended Feb 2026) results showed consolidated revenue of JPY10.43trn (down from JPY11.97trn) largely reflecting the YORK/Seven Bank deconsolidations; North American same-store merchandise sales declined and 7-Eleven Inc. chain sales fell 7.3%; domestic Japan CVS operating income continued its multi-year drift down to JPY222.5bn.

Executed roughly JPY600 billion in share buybacks under an April 2025-February 2026 authorization (up to 400 million shares / JPY600bn), lifting treasury stock to ~JPY615bn and cutting shares outstanding from ~2,598M (FY2025) to ~2,312M (Q1 FY2027, post the March 2024 3-for-1 split).

Raised FY2027 (ending Feb 2027) group guidance to roughly JPY425bn operating profit and JPY10.4trn revenue after a stronger-than-expected Q1, aided by higher North American fuel margins; the North American IPO timeline was pushed back to fiscal 2027 at the earliest, and the North Star plan (store closures/remodels, expanded franchising) was accelerated.
Q2 FY2027 operating income of JPY127.2bn beat consensus (~JPY124.1bn), but net income of JPY63.8bn missed estimates; full-year FY2027 operating profit guidance of JPY425bn was maintained.

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Stephen Dacus has emphasized that higher energy prices are squeezing North American consumers and that sustained high gasoline prices could further reduce store traffic; management describes the Transformation Plan and North Star plan as the vehicle for rebuilding momentum and execution discipline after years of slowing innovation, while reiterating commitment to the multi-year capital return program.

bull_case: Post-restructuring, Seven & i is now a cleaner, pure-play global convenience-store business, removing the conglomerate discount associated with superstores and banking that activists (ValueAct) and Couche-Tard both argued was masking value

Large, ongoing buyback program (JPY600bn in FY2026 alone, reducing shares outstanding materially since the 2024 split) is shrinking the share count and supporting EPS growth even if operating profit is flat

Dominant, highly profitable domestic franchise royalty model in Japan (7-Eleven, Lawson, FamilyMart control ~90% of the market) provides a stable, high-margin cash engine to fund the North American turnaround

North Star transformation plan (store remodels, franchising expansion, portfolio rationalization) plus a potential North American IPO offer a credible path to re-rating the overseas business if execution improves
New, more shareholder-oriented management under CEO Stephen Dacus and separated Chair/CEO roles signal improved governance and capital discipline following the Couche-Tard episode
bear_case: North American convenience and fuel business remains structurally challenged -- same-store merchandise sales declining, chain sales down 7.3% in FY2026, and share loss to larger-format competitors (Wawa, Sheetz, Buc-ee's, Casey's)

Deconsolidation of YORK Holdings and Seven Bank breaks balance-sheet and income-statement continuity (cash fell from JPY1.35trn to JPY426bn; total assets from JPY11.4trn to JPY9.1trn), complicating valuation and creating a messy multi-year comparison base for investors and models

Domestic Japan convenience-store profitability has been quietly eroding for several years (operating income down from JPY250.5bn in FY2024 to JPY222.5bn in FY2026) even as the company touts the segment as its crown jewel
North American IPO -- a key value-unlocking catalyst -- has already been delayed to FY2027 at the earliest, raising execution-risk and timeline-risk concerns

Large capital return commitments (buybacks, reinvestment in YORK's successor entity) reduce balance-sheet flexibility just as the company needs capital for store remodels, fresh-food investment and North American M&A
